title: nerDDocs
about: An open-source docs platform where a slider on each page switches its text between levels.

branches.name: v1.0.0
branches.holds: Learn what readers and authors need, pick the tech stack, design and build the first features, and publish nerDDocs to npm.

items.name: Product idea
items.why: What nerDDocs is, and how it should feel for readers and authors, guides each design.
items.doneWhen: The idea of nerDDocs is set: each page holds its text at several levels, and a slider on the page switches between them.

items.name: Use cases
items.why: The tech stack and the designs come from the use cases.
items.doneWhen: Every reader, author, team and AI tool use case is listed, each with an example.

items.name: Tech stack
items.why: The stack is picked only once all use cases are known.
items.doneWhen: A doc names each part of the stack and the use cases that need it.

items.name: Docs app design
items.why: The UI and UX of the app for v1.0.0 come from a vision of all that nerDDocs should be, and leave room for the later versions. The vision, the UX and the tool that makes the mock are approved before the mock is made.
items.doneWhen: The mock of the app is approved after the rounds of feedback.

items.name: Docs app code
items.why: The docs app works as designed. The contents panel hides, and a section with subsections has an expand and collapse arrow.
items.doneWhen: npx nerddocs shows a docs folder as a site, and a saved change shows on the site.

items.name: Docs app tests
items.why: Tests for the docs app, so a change cannot break it unseen.
items.doneWhen: npm test checks the docs app, as designed.

items.name: Level slider design
items.why: A slider on each page changes the level. The slider shows the name and the icon of the level, a faint mark shows the level of each part, and the slider works with the keyboard and a screen reader. The slider sits in a panel at the bottom of the page, and a tab on the panel hides it. When the level changes, the text animates, the reader's place holds, and a soft tint shows what changed.
items.doneWhen: A mock of the level slider on a docs page is reviewed and approved.

items.name: Level slider code
items.why: The level slider works on the pages of the docs app, as in the approved mock. The file nerddocs.json lists the name and the icon of each level, and a fence such as ::: overview internals marks the text of those levels.
items.doneWhen: A docs folder with marked text shows the slider in npx nerddocs, and each move changes the text and holds the place, with 3 levels, with 8 levels and on a long page.

items.name: Level slider tests
items.why: Tests for the level slider, so a change cannot break it unseen.
items.doneWhen: npm test checks the level slider, as designed.

items.name: Swap by level design
items.why: Each level can hold a text of its own for a part, so moving to another level replaces text, not only adds or hides it. The level marks leave plain colons in text, such as `file:line`, as written. A fence counts only when nerddocs.json lists all its words, and a page shows what happens when the file is missing or broken, or when a page has no levels.
items.doneWhen: A mock of the nerddocs.json cases on a docs page is reviewed and approved.

items.name: Swap by level code
items.why: The docs app works as in the approved mock. A fence with a word that nerddocs.json does not list stays text. A missing or broken file opens a modal with 'Don't show again', and `"levels": false` turns the slider off with no modal. In a run with uneven parts, the part on the reader's line changes into its new text. A heading with no text at the current level hides.
items.doneWhen: npx nerddocs shows each case of the mock on a docs folder, and a page with 1 part at one level and 3 parts at another holds the reader's place on a move from any of the 3.

items.name: Swap by level tests
items.why: Tests for swap by level, so a change cannot break it unseen.
items.doneWhen: npm test checks swap by level, as designed.

items.name: Read time design
items.why: The page shows how long the current level takes to read and changes the time as the reader moves the slider. A box shows the time of each level for the page and for all pages. The speed fits English by default, and nerddocs.json can set another speed.
items.doneWhen: A mock of the read time on a docs page is reviewed and approved.

items.name: Read time code
items.why: The read time works as in the approved mock. Each stop shows its time under its name. A clock button opens a box with the time of each level for the page and for all pages. With the panel hidden, or on a page with no levels, the time shows next to the title. The key wordsPerMinute in nerddocs.json sets the speed.
items.doneWhen: npx nerddocs shows each case of the mock on a docs folder, and a saved change to a page updates the times of that page and the 'All pages' times on another open page.

items.name: Read time tests
items.why: Tests for the read time, so a change cannot break it unseen.
items.doneWhen: npm test checks the read time, as designed.

items.name: Level memory design
items.why: A defaults button opens a box where the reader sets a default level. Moving the slider changes the level of the current page only. After a change, a chip shows the old level icon and the new level icon, with one 'All pages' button that applies the new level to all pages. A modal lists the pages that would lose their own level.
items.doneWhen: A mock of the level memory on a docs page is reviewed and approved.

items.name: Level memory code
items.why: The level memory works as in the approved mock. A page keeps its level on a reload, a tree click and back, in the current tab. 'All pages' and the 'Defaults' box set the default level, and a modal lists the pages that would change. A page without the wanted level opens at the nearest lower level, or else the nearest higher one.
items.doneWhen: npx nerddocs shows each case of the level memory as in the approved mock.

items.name: Level memory tests
items.why: Tests for the level memory, so a change cannot break it unseen.
items.doneWhen: npm test checks the level memory, as designed.

items.name: Theme brainstorm
items.why: This step sets which themes exist, what each one is called, and how far each one changes the page.
items.doneWhen: Each theme has a name and an approved look, and a track of its own in 'Theme looks'.

items.name: Themes design
items.why: A 'Themes' button opens a box with a search, a list of the themes of 'Theme looks', a 'Light | Dark | System' switch and a preview of a sample page in the selected theme and look. 'Apply' shows them on the page and keeps them, and 'Cancel' changes nothing. 'System' shows the light or the dark look to match the computer. A theme changes the colors, the fonts, the art behind the text and the look of the slider. The layout and the text animation are the same in every theme. The text sits on a solid area, and the art behind it stays still.
items.doneWhen: The theme box on a docs page is reviewed and approved.

items.name: Themes code
items.why: The theme button and the theme box work as designed. Each theme is a folder of src/themes/, and a contributor adds one by the steps in CONTRIBUTING.md.
items.doneWhen: npx nerddocs shows each theme in its light and dark look, and a picked theme and look hold on every page and after a reload.

items.name: Themes tests
items.why: Tests for the themes, so a change cannot break them unseen. Each theme in src/themes/ is checked with no test of its own.
items.doneWhen: npm test checks the themes and the theme box, as designed.

items.name: Text width design
items.why: The text narrows with the window down to a limit, and past that limit the text area scrolls sideways. The text widens with the window up to a default width. A ruler that the reader turns on widens the text as far as the window allows.

items.name: Page content design
items.why: Pages show Mermaid diagrams, code with syntax colors, wide tables, box diagrams, light and dark images, HTML wireframes, an OpenAPI reference and an outline of the page. Box diagrams need a monospace font file to keep their lines joined.

items.name: Dimensions design
items.why: An author splits the docs into dimensions, such as 'User guide', 'Administration' and 'Legal', each with its own pages. One set of levels applies to all of the docs.

items.name: Topic tree design
items.why: A tree lists the topics, and levels replace only the depth from overview to low level.

items.name: Part ids design
items.why: An author gives a part an id, and any page links to the part by its id. A part written once shows on many pages.

items.name: Search by level design
items.why: Search hits and links open the page at the level of what they point to.

items.name: Page links design
items.why: A link icon copies a link to the page at the current level and at the reader's place. It needs links that open a page at a level, so it comes after 'Search by level'. The foot of each page links to the previous page and the next page.

items.name: Author preview design
items.why: Authors see the page at each level.

items.name: Author checks design
items.why: A check lists broken links, pages with a heading and no text, and text that breaks when a part is hidden.

items.name: Author skill design
items.why: A Claude skill helps authors write new nerDDocs docs and move existing Markdown docs into nerDDocs. Each moved page reads right at every level.

items.name: Static export design
items.why: One command writes the docs as plain files. They open from disk with no server and no internet, for teams in air-gapped networks. The same files can be uploaded to any static host and linked from a landing page.

items.name: Static export code
items.why: The export writes the same pages that the docs app shows.

items.name: Publish to npm
items.why: nerDDocs is a public npm package, so a project runs it with npx nerddocs.

items.name: Release v1.0.0
items.why: v1.0.0 is out when each feature of v1.0.0 is designed, built and tested, and nerDDocs is on npm.
items.doneWhen: master holds v1.0.0 with the tag v1.0.0, and the release of v1.0.0 is reviewed and approved.

branches.name: v1.1.0
branches.holds: The glossary, backlinks, AI access, the MCP server, versions, languages, hidden files, video and GIF support, custom levels and the in-app editor.

items.name: Glossary design
items.why: An author defines a term once, and a reader sees its meaning by hovering over or tapping the term. Docs often define the same term on several pages.

items.name: Backlinks design
items.why: Under a part, the reader sees the list of pages that link to it.

items.name: AI access design
items.why: AI tools read the docs at a level they choose, through an llms.txt file and a Markdown copy of each page at each level.

items.name: MCP server design
items.why: An MCP server in the nerDDocs app lets AI coding tools search and read the docs at a chosen level.

items.name: Versions design
items.why: Readers switch between the docs of each product version.

items.name: Languages design
items.why: The docs come in several languages, and the reader picks one. Each language can set its own reading speed for the read time, and a language with no speed of its own uses the default speed. A language with no spaces between words, such as Chinese, counts characters in place of words.

items.name: Hidden files design
items.why: A team keeps chosen files, such as the notes in drafts/, out of the published site.

items.name: Video and GIF design
items.why: Pages show videos and GIFs, and each one adds to the read time. A video can be skipped, so a page with 10 minutes of text and a 5-minute video shows the range '10-15m'.

items.name: Custom levels design
items.why: A page can have levels of its own, in place of the one set of levels of the docs. This needs its own design and decisions.

items.name: In-app editor design
items.why: Authors edit pages in the nerDDocs app, and the editor saves to the same Markdown files. The editor edits glossary terms and the pages of each version and language, so it waits for those designs.
